assignments.name: regulatory_text
assignments.value:
GDPR Article 13-14 — Information to be provided (transparency)
  When a customer-support AI feature collects personal data from a user,
  the data controller must inform the individual, at the time data is
  collected, of: the identity of the controller, the purpose of processing,
  the legal basis, retention period, and the individual's rights (access,
  rectification, erasure, objection). Plain-language implication for a
  support chatbot: if it captures account/contact details during a
  conversation, the product needs a clear, accessible disclosure of what's
  collected and why — not buried in a general privacy policy only.

GDPR Article 13-14 — Information to be provided (transparency)
  When a customer-support AI feature collects personal data from a user,
  the data controller must inform the individual, at the time data is
  collected, of: the identity of the controller, the purpose of processing,
  the legal basis, retention period, and the individual's rights (access,
  rectification, erasure, objection). Plain-language implication for a
  support chatbot: if it captures account/contact details during a
  conversation, the product needs a clear, accessible disclosure of what's
  collected and why — not buried in a general privacy policy only.

  GDPR Article 22 — Automated individual decision-making, including
  profiling
  Individuals have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely
  on automated processing (including profiling) that produces legal effects
  or similarly significantly affects them, subject to certain exceptions
  (explicit consent, contract necessity, or authorizing law) — and even
  then, the controller must provide a way to obtain human intervention,
  express their point of view, and contest the decision. Plain-language
  implication: if the support AI's output can materially affect a user
  (e.g., autonomously denying a refund or account action with no human
  review path), this article is implicated and a human-in-the-loop path is
  required.

  EU AI Act — Transparency obligations for AI systems interacting with
  natural persons (Article 50)
  Providers must ensure that natural persons are informed they are
  interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from context.
  Plain-language implication: a customer-support chatbot must disclose to
  the end user that they're talking to an AI, not a human agent, unless
  that's already unmistakably clear from the interface.
